title: Compute signal synthesis and procurement queue
content:
Purpose:

Quick working notes to convert telemetry signals (burn, tail latency, hot routes) into an actionable procurement queue and recommended SKU blend for the next 6–12 months. Intention is to capture heuristics and edge-case rules we use when prioritizing orders and to surface tradeoffs for PM/finance reviews.

Context and problem statement:
- We have highly variable per-region burn due to PLG customers and bursty real-time workloads.
- Current ordering cadence (quarterly large tranches) exposes us to long-lead risk and SKU mismatch for short-lived projects.
- Need a reproducible mapping from signals -> order priority, plus fallback lanes for lead-time slippage.

Signals we ingest (raw):
- 7d/30d token burn by region (api tokens/day)
- P95 model latency by region and model family
- Instance fill rate (reserved vs spot vs spare pool) by AZ
- Active canary/rollout capacity delta (extra headroom needed for canaries)
- Fleet age distribution (months-in-service histogram)

Derived signals (heuristics):
1) Urgency score = 0.6*(30d burn growth rate) + 0.3*(P95 latency delta above SLO) + 0.1*(reserved capacity shortfall fraction)
2) SKU-fit index = weighted demand for fp16 vs int8 inference profiles per model family
3) Flexibility score = fraction of workloads compatible with multi-arch (supports older gen)

Example numbers (region us-west-2, snapshot 2025-01-01):
- 30d burn growth: +42%
- P95 latency delta: 18ms over SLO (SLO=110ms)
- reserved shortfall: 9%
- computed urgency score: 0.6*0.42 + 0.3*0.163 + 0.1*0.09 ≈ 0.315 (ranked high)

SKU blend rationale (principles):
- Mix for predictability: 60% mid-range T-class (economy per-token, good for caching-heavy workloads), 30% H-class (high mem for long-context LLMs), 10% experimental/accelerator (latest gen for latency-sensitive customers).
- Avoid overconcentration: cap any single SKU to 45% in a region to reduce single-sku lead-time exposure.
- Prefer families with mature supply pipelines if lead times > 10 weeks.

Order prioritization rules (pipeline):
1) Immediate (place now): region urgency > 0.25 OR reserved shortfall > 15% AND lead time < 12 weeks.
2) Staged (plan within 4 weeks): urgency 0.12–0.25 OR fleet age median > 30 months.
3) Strategic (quarterly review): urgency < 0.12 and flexibility score > 0.6.

Lead-time layering and hedges:
- Primary lane: 12–20 week manufacturer lead time for targeted SKU.
- Secondary lane: 6–10 week of compatible alternative SKU (different mem/throughput tradeoffs) to meet short-term spikes.
- Tertiary lane: spot/lease short-term capacity (cloud partners, on-demand hosts) to cover immediate 2–6 week gaps.

Arrival scenario table (text):
- Best: full shipment on time -> deploy into reserved pools -> immediate latency relief for hot routes.
- Partial: 60–80% arrives -> prioritize H-class -> reassign mid-range capacity for caching workloads.
- Late: >4 weeks slip -> activate tertiary lane -> raise canary thresholds to reduce reserved capacity pressure.

Cost vs risk notes:
- Hedging with alternative SKUs increases unit cost by ~8–15% but reduces outage risk.
- Over-provisioning by 10% in a single region costs ~12% in monthly $ but buys breathing room for bursty PLG usage.

Operational checklist for each order:
- Confirm SKU fit with serving runtime (quantization/compat flags) — owner: infra-runtime
- Validate power/cooling footprint in target DC — owner: facilities
- Create rollout plan mapping to canary groups (A/B route percentages) — owner: platform
- Create contingency PR (secondary SKU) with finance approval for price delta >5%

Open questions and tradeoffs to surface to PM/Finance:
- How much multi-region buffer should finance fund vs ops? Current proposal: 8% cross-region buffer funded centrally.
- Tolerance for single-SKU concentration in exchange for unit price discounts from vendor.
- Acceptable latency SLO drift during partial arrivals (max 15% API latency degradation for up to 10 days?).

Immediate action items (next 2 weeks):
- Run compute-signal job over last 90 days and produce per-region urgency ranking (owner: Samir)
- Simulate 3 arrival scenarios for top 5 regions and estimate cost delta (owner: Jin)
- Draft finance ask for a 8% cross-region buffer allocation and present in weekly ops review (owner: Ava)

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally succinct — will expand into a spreadsheet with per-SKU unit economics and a calendar view once the urgency ranking lands.
- I expect the SKU-blend percentages to shift by region; EMEA tends to want higher H-class due to longer-context clients.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-10: initial sketch and heuristics
- 2025-01-22: added order prioritization thresholds after sync with platform team
- 2025-02-03: updated cost hedge numbers after procurement call

References and useful links:
- "fleet-age-analytics" (confluence) for histogram queries
- procurement playbook (internal) for vendor negotiation templates
- JIRA-ENGINF-412 for the current ordering ticket queue

End of note.
